questions.q: This sign is a warning sign indicating uneven road surfaces.
Trams are not considered automobiles.
The maximum load capacity of an ordinary vehicle is 500 kg.
questions.explanation: The maximum load capacity is specified in the vehicle registration document.

questions.q: An ordinary license allows driving a vehicle with a capacity of 11 passengers.
questions.explanation: A medium license is required for vehicles with 11 or more passengers.

questions.q: The maximum speed on a vehicle-only road without a specified speed limit is 100 km/h.
questions.explanation: The maximum speed is 60 km/h.

questions.q: During a medium license suspension period, you can still drive a motorized bicycle.
questions.explanation: Driving any vehicle, including motorized bicycles, is prohibited during a license suspension.

questions.q: Driving with a heavy load increases braking distance.
Wearing a seatbelt is mandatory when reversing a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Seatbelt use is exempted when reversing.

questions.q: A medium license is required to drive a vehicle with a maximum load capacity of 4 tons.
questions.explanation: A non-restricted quasi-medium license is also sufficient.

questions.q: The brakes of a motorcycle have interconnected front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The front and rear brakes operate independently.

questions.q: This sign indicates a bicycle crossing lane.
Driving with an expired license is considered unlicensed driving.
If cargo falls onto a highway, you should request its removal via an emergency telephone.
The minimum speed for large motorcycles on the main lanes of expressways is 30 km/h.
questions.explanation: The minimum speed is 50 km/h.

questions.q: Stopping to wait for cargo or for passengers to board or alight is considered parking.
questions.explanation: Stopping to wait for cargo is parking, but stopping for passengers is considered stopping, not parking.

questions.q: In a no-overtaking zone, overtaking a motorized bicycle with an automobile is also prohibited.
On slippery roads, it is preferable to brake intermittently to reduce speed.
When starting an automatic vehicle, shift the gear lever to 'D' without pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: The brake pedal must be firmly pressed when shifting to 'D'.

questions.q: When driving, wearing sandals or high heels is prohibited as they may interfere with driving.
The maximum speed for large special vehicles on general roads is 60 km/h.
This sign indicates a horn-use zone, where vehicles and trams must sound their horns.
When driving at night on busy roads, it is advisable to switch headlights to low beam.
Overtaking a vehicle that is overtaking a motorized bicycle or light vehicle does not constitute double overtaking.
As speed increases, stopping distance lengthens, but braking distance shortens.
questions.explanation: Both stopping and braking distances increase with speed.

questions.q: Police motorcycles are not considered emergency vehicles.
questions.explanation: Police motorcycles are included as emergency vehicles.

questions.q: Trams must proceed slowly at locations with this sign.
Carts or rickshaws are considered automobiles.
questions.explanation: Carts and rickshaws are classified as light vehicles, not automobiles.

questions.q: When calculating passenger capacity, three children under 12 years old are counted as two adults.
The legal speed limit for ordinary motorcycles or motorized bicycles of 125cc or less when towing another vehicle is 25 km/h.
A steep slope refers to a gradient of approximately 10% (about 6 degrees) or more.
A priority road is one with this sign or a road with a lane or center line extending into an intersection.
Overtaking is allowed near road curves if visibility is clear.
questions.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited near curves regardless of visibility.

questions.q: If the vehicle ahead is overtaking a motorized bicycle, overtaking that vehicle does not constitute double overtaking.
A U-turn refers to reversing a vehicle.
questions.explanation: A U-turn refers to turning the vehicle around to go in the opposite direction.

questions.q: You must be at least 20 years old and have held a motorcycle license for at least 3 years to carry a passenger on a motorcycle on general roads.
questions.explanation: The requirement is 1 year for general roads; 3 years applies to highways.

questions.q: This sign prohibits vehicles from crossing to the right but allows crossing to the left side of the road.
If a tire punctures while driving, hold the steering wheel firmly, correct the vehicle’s direction, shift to a low gear to reduce speed, and brake intermittently.
Using the horn for greetings is prohibited.
When driving in fog, use high-beam headlights and follow the center line or the tail lights of the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Low-beam headlights should be used to prevent glare from reflection.

questions.q: When starting an automatic vehicle, the gear lever should be in 'N' or 'P'.
questions.explanation: The gear lever must be in 'P' when starting.

questions.q: In an automatic vehicle, if the gear lever is not in 'P' or 'N', the vehicle may move slowly even without pressing the accelerator, a phenomenon called creep.
When a vehicle’s speed doubles, the centrifugal force also doubles.
questions.explanation: Centrifugal force is proportional to the square of the speed, so it increases fourfold.

questions.q: Tire pressure for highway driving should be slightly lower.
questions.explanation: Tire pressure should be slightly higher for highway driving.

questions.q: If cargo falls onto the main lane of a highway, stop the vehicle and remove the cargo yourself immediately.
questions.explanation: Use an emergency telephone to request cargo removal.

questions.q: In principle, parking is prohibited if there is less than 3.5 meters of clearance on the right side of the road.
When the road is wet, the reaction distance increases.
questions.explanation: The braking distance increases on wet roads, not the reaction distance.

questions.q: At a railway crossing with a signal, stopping or checking for safety is not necessary.
questions.explanation: Safety checks are still required even with a signal.

questions.q: When passing on a narrow slope, the downhill vehicle must stop temporarily to yield to the uphill vehicle.
When passing on a slope with a passing bay, the vehicle on the side with the passing bay must yield, regardless of whether it is going uphill or downhill.
When driving at night, keep your gaze as close as possible to monitor road conditions.
questions.explanation: Look as far ahead as possible to detect obstacles early.
